texts.preamble: Rajesha.A.S vs Mallikarjuna Service Station on 15 July, 2025 Kabc020146452023 Before Motor Vehicles Accident Claims Tribunal, Bengaluru City Scch-17
texts.facts: On 04.04.2023 at about 11.30 p.m., the petitioners were proceeding as inmates of the Car bearing No. KA.41.MA.1358 from Hassan to Bengaluru, when the Car reached near Didaga under bridge, NH-75, B M road, at that time the driver of the Petrol Tanker bearing No. KA.46.8838 which was proceeding ahead of the Car, which was proceeding at high speed, in a rash and negligent manner, the driver of the said tanker without observing any traffic rules and regulations applied sudden break without giving any indication. As such the driver of the Car hit to the back portion of the tanker and caused the accident. Due to the impact the Car crushed severely and all the petitioners who were inmates of the car sustained grievous injuries. Immediately after the accident, the petitioner in MVC 3128/2023, 3129/2023, 3126/2023 and 3127/2023 were shifted to Adichunchanagiri hospital & reserarch centre, Mandya, wherein the petitioners took treatment as an inpatients. The each petitioners have spent more than Rs.1,00,000/- towards medical and other allowances. Rajesha. At the time of accident, the petitioner of MVC 3128/2023 was hale and healthy, working at Kanthi Sweets and earning Rs.20,000/- per month. Due to the accidental injuries, the petitioner is not able to continue with the work and lost his earning capacity. At the time of accident, the petitioner in MVC 3126/2023 and 3129/2023 were hale and healthy, doing tailoring work and each were earning Rs.15,000/- per month. Due to the accidental injuries, the petitioners are not able to continue with the work and lost their earning capacity. SCCH-17 6 MVC No. 3128/2023 C/w 3126/2023, 3127/2023 & 3129/20233 At the time of accident, the petitioner in MVC No.3127/2023 was hale and healthy, aged about 7 years and studying in 2nd standard. Due to the accidental injuries, the petitioner is not able to concentrate on her studies and personal work. The respondent No.1 is the owner and respondent No.2 being the insurer of the Tanker bearing No. KA.46.8838 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioners. 3. After service of notices both the respondents have appeared through their respective counsels, but respondent No.1 owner has not filed written statement. The respondent No.2 insurance company has filed its written statement by denying the cause and manner of accident and also the involvement of the offending Tanker Rajesha.A.S vs Mallikarjuna Service Station on 15 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/72598065/ 4 bearing No. KA.46.8838 in the alleged accident. Further it has denied the issuance of policy to the offending Tanker bearing No. KA.46.8838. It is contended that there is no SCCH-17 7 MVC No. 3128/2023 C/w 3126/2023, 3127/2023 & 3129/20233 compliance of Sec.134(c) of MA Act. Further it has contended that, the driver of the Car bearing No. KA.41.MA.1358 has not maintained safe distance and contributed towards the cause of accident and also the driver of the said Car was not having valid driving license as on the date of accident. Also contended that, the driver of the offending Tanker bearing No. KA.46.8838 was not having valid driving license and also the vehicle was also not having valid FC and permit as on the date of accident. Further it has denied the age, occupation and income of the petitioners. The compensation claimed by the petitioners is too excessive, exorbitant. Accordingly, respondent No.2 prays to dismiss the petition against it. 4. On the basis of rival contention, the following issues have been framed : ISSUES IN MVC No.3128/2023, 3127/2023, 3126/2023 and 3129/2023 1. Whether the petitioners proves that, the accident occurred due to rash SCCH-17 8 MVC No. 3128/2023 C/w 3126/2023, 3127/2023 & 3129/20233 and negligent act of driving of Petrol Tanker bearing No. KA.46.8838 as as a result, they have sustained in- juries? 5. As per order dated 21.02.2024 by considering the same cause of action, MVC No.3126/2023, MVC No.3127/2023, MVC No.3129/2023 were clubbed with MVC 3128/2023 for common trial from the stage of evidence. 6. In order to prove the claim petition, the petitioners lead common evidence in MVC No. 3128/2023 and examined themselves as PW.1 to PW.4 and got marked the documents at Ex.P1 to 31. SCCH-17 9 MVC No. 3128/2023 C/w 3126/2023, 3127/2023 & 3129/20233 On the other hand, the driver of the offending Petrol Tanker bearing No. KA.46.8838 is examined as RW.1 and Ex.R1 is got marked. Further the official of 2 nd respondent company is examined as RW.2 and got marked the documents at Ex.R2 to R5, but the evidence of RW.2 is discarded as per Order dated 17.03.2025. Thereafter the new official of 2nd respondent company is examined as RW.3 and the document is got marked at Ex.R6. 7. Rajesha.A.S vs Mallikarjuna Service Station on 15 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/72598065/ 6 8. My findings on the above issues are as under. ISSUES IN MVC. 3128/2023, 3126/2023, 3127/2023 & 3129/2023. Issue No.1: In the affirmative, Issue No.2: In the Partly affirmative by holding that the petitioners proved their age and failed to SCCH-17 10 MVC No. 3128/2023 C/w 3126/2023, 3127/2023 & 3129/20233 prove the exact income as pleaded in the petition. Issue No.3: In the affirmative, Issue No.4: As per final orders for the following.- REASONS ISSUE NO.1 IN ALL THE CASES: 9. The petitioners to prove their claim have produced true copies of FIR, complaint, crime details form, spot sketch, IMV report, wound certificate, charge sheet, notice and reply to the notice U/Sec.133 which are marked under Ex.P.1 to 7. 10. As per the documents produced by the petitioner Ex.P1- FIR is came to be registered on the basis of first information given by one Pushpalatha who is the wife of the driver of the offending Petrol Tanker bearing No. KA.46.8838. In the said complaint, the first informant alleged the rash and negligent driving by the driver of Petrol Tanker bearing No. KA.46.8838. After SCCH-17 11 MVC No. 3128/2023 C/w 3126/2023, 3127/2023 & 3129/20233 Rajesha.A.S vs Mallikarjuna Service Station on 15 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/72598065/ 7 registration of FIR the IO has prepared spot mahazar and spot sketch as per Ex.P3. 11. The respondent No.2 insurance company seriously disputed the fact of negligence of the driver of offending Petrol Tanker bearing No. KA.46.8838 and examined the driver of the said tractor by denying his negligence. The driver who is the eye witness to the accident denied his negligence and deposed before this tribunal that the driver of the Car bearing No. KA.41.MA.1358 came in rash and negligent manner and dashed against the rare side of the Petrol Tanker and caused the accident. Thereby even though the crime records alleges the negligence of the driver of Petrol Tanker bearing No. KA.46.8838, the said driver appeared himself before this tribunal and denied his negligence. 12 . Immediately after the accident, the IO conducted spot mahazar and rough sketch as per Ex.P3. The petitioner admitted to the hospital for the injuries sustained by him, which might certainly have deprived him of the basic comforts and enjoyment. To sum up the above discussion, the petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following Towards pain and sufferings - Rs. 50,000/- Medical expenses - Rs. 10,400/- Towards diet, food, - Rs. 20,000/- nourishment, attendant and conveyance charges Towards loss of future earning - NIL capacity Loss of income during laid up - NIL period Due to loss of amenities and - Rs. 25,000/- enjoyment of life Total - Rs. 1,05,400/- SCCH-17 26 MVC No. 3128/2023 C/w 3126/2023, 3127/2023 & 3129/20233 ISSUE NO.2 & 3 IN MVC NO.3126/2023: 25. Hence, the petitioner is entitle for compensation.
texts.arguments: It is necessary to reassert that in a claim for compensation filed under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, the claimant is expected to prove the incident on basis of principle of preponderance of probabilities and the view taken by this Court is fortified by the decision rendered by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Kusum and others V/s Satbir and others which is reported in 2011 SAR (CIVIL) 319. Further the Hon'ble Supreme Court in case of Bimla Devi and others v. Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others reported in (2009) 13 SCC 530 has observed that, it is necessary to be borne in mind that strict proof of an accident caused by a particular bus in a particular manner may not be possible to be done by the claimants. Further the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in National Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Krishnappa and another reported in 2001 ACJ 1105, where the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka considering the fact that the rider of the offending vehicle was not examined to prove any contributory negligence on the part of scooterist held that the accident had occurred due to rash or negligent driving by the rider of the offending van. In the same manner the petitioner also not produced any evidence and not examined his employer to establish that after the accident he was on leave and on bed rest, as such he has not received any salary. In the judgment reported in 2020(4) KCCR 2621 between Sri Nandish K. V/s United India Insurance Co. Ltd. & another wherein it is held that, no compensation SCCH-17 24 MVC No. 3128/2023 C/w 3126/2023, 3127/2023 & 3129/20233 could be awarded towards the loss of earning capacity if physical disability do not effect claimant's capacity to work. No expert evidence is also available to hold that the petitioner sustained physical permanent disabilities. The answers given by the petitioner evidentiates that the petitioner is continuing his work and no disability is caused which effects his earning capacity. Hence, this court has no option but to hold that the petitioner has not suffered any permanent physical disability which has resulted in reduction of his salary and hence he is not entitled for any compensation under this head. The petitioner also not made out any evidence or grounds to hold that he sustained the loss of income during the laid down period. Hence, in the absence of any evidence, petitioner is not entitled for any amount under the head of loss of income during laid up period and disability. 26 . The petitioner has produced wound certificate as per Ex.P15 which shows that the petitioner sustained Rajesha.A.S vs Mallikarjuna Service Station on 15 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/72598065/ 18 four injuries, which are grievous in nature. The petitioner has not examined the doctor who treated the petitioner at the time of accident. Without the evidence of doctor, it is not possible to believe that, the petitioner has sustained disability due to grievous injuries. 27 . According to the petitioner she was doing tailoring work and was earning Rs.15,000/- p.m. In the judgment reported in 2020(4) KCCR 2621 between Sri Nandish K. V/s United India Insurance Co. Ltd. & another wherein it is held that, no compensation could be awarded towards the loss of earning capacity if physical disability do not effect claimant's capacity to work. By applying the said precedent, this court has no option but to hold that the petitioner has not suffered any permanent physical disability which has resulted in reduction of his salary and hence she is not entitled for any compensation under this head.
